label: Bible Study
prompt: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to _____.
verse: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
note: A saying of Jesus preserved outside the Gospels — Paul quotes it from memory in Acts.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: If any of you lack _____, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
verse: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
note: God gives wisdom 'liberally, and upbraideth not' — no lecture attached to the gift.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And the LORD said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's _____?
verse: And the LORD said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?
note: Cain's deflection became the world's most famous rhetorical question — and the answer is yes.

label: Deep Water
prompt: The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the LORD hath his way in the _____ and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
verse: The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the LORD hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
note: Nahum to Nineveh: God's patience is not indifference — even the storm is his footpath.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and _____ of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.
verse: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.
note: 'Superfluity of naughtiness' — overflowing leftover wickedness. The KJV at its most quotable.
